description:
Workspace V&V rule: methodology and results, both, in the doc comment where a reader meets the test.

What can honestly be checked here:
  - overall material balance closes (sum of cuts == feed) to a stated tolerance
  - cut boiling ranges land in the conventional bands (naphtha/kero/diesel/AGO) — a sanity band, not an accuracy claim
  - the pseudo-component slate reproduces the bulk API gravity it was generated from (round-trip)
  - black-oil correlation outputs sit inside their published validity ranges for the chosen crude

What CANNOT be claimed and must be said so: this is not validated against a real refinery CDU or a published assay-to-yield dataset. State the absence explicitly rather than letting green tests imply validation. No human V&V.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Done — V&V documentation is in the test doc comments, methodology and measured results together, per the workspace rule.

What IS checked, with numbers recorded where the reader meets the test:
  * API <-> SG round-trip inverse to <1e-12
  * bulk properties in crude-like ranges (38 degAPI -> SG 0.8348, MW 206.5 g/mol, NBP 538.8 K)
  * a heavier crude (22 degAPI) characterises as heavier on all three properties
  * pseudo-component slate normalises to 1 within 1e-9, boiling points 390-825 K
  * CrudeCut bands tile the temperature axis with no gaps or overlaps
  * config validation rejects five specific mistakes, each with its own error variant
  * column-basis split fractions partition unity to <1e-12
  * the full column converges (38 it, 6.7e-7) to a MONOTONIC profile with draw temperatures 423.6 / 494.9 / 511.7 / 530.8 / 588.5 K

What is explicitly NOT claimed, stated in the module header and again in the test:
  * no comparison against a real CDU, a published assay-to-yield dataset, or DWSIM itself
  * the pseudo-component slate is a DISTRIBUTION ASSUMPTION from two bulk numbers, not a measured assay; two crudes with the same API and mean NBP can have quite different TBP curves and yields
  * no stripping steam, no pump-arounds, no furnace, no vacuum tower — the energy balance is not a refinery's
  * the CDU-band agreement of the draw temperatures is a SANITY check, not a validation

No human V&V is claimed.

title: crude: V&V — document methodology AND measured numbers

description:
The shared core every other child needs. raffles today has distributions, samplers (MonteCarlo/LatinHypercube/Grid), sensitivity and surrogate -- but NO likelihood, prior/posterior, or any Bayesian machinery (verified: grep for mcmc/bayes/metropolis/likelihood hits only lib.rs prose).

Reuse raffles' existing Distribution enum for priors -- do not introduce a
parallel type. Follow the workspace rules: enum dispatch, no Box<dyn>/&dyn, no
lifetime params, uom where a physical quantity crosses the boundary.

Deliver: prior/posterior/likelihood types, log-density evaluation, and the trait
contract a model-updating problem implements. This is the interface every
sampler below plugs into, so get it reviewed before building on it.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: LANDED, verified 2026-09-17: crates/raffles/src/bayesian/mod.rs delivers IndependentPrior (independent marginals from raffles::distributions, -inf outside support), log-density evaluation, and the mcmc/transitional modules that consume it as the trait contract this bead asked for. Not linked when written -- bn was unavailable in that session's container. See the consolidated comment on op-dwqw (parent) for the full landing and the licensing caveat. Not closing unilaterally: no human V&V sign-off yet and this is Adolphus Lye's crate to steer, but the described deliverable exists in the tree.

title: Bayesian inference foundation in raffles: likelihood, prior, posterior

description:
MEASURED 2026-09-11 by verification case 8 (crates/farrer-park/tests/locking.rs, shear_locking_in_quad4_is_measured_and_bbar_does_not_cure_it), which replaced the unmeasured claim in op-vrtt.1.

THE NUMBERS. Quad4 cantilever, nu = 0, deflection at the mid-height node of the loaded edge, against Timoshenko beam theory (below 1 = too stiff):

L/H = 8, square elements:
  ny = 2  (102 dofs)  full 0.8875  B-bar 0.9579
  ny = 4  (330 dofs)  full 0.9692  B-bar 0.9890
  ny = 8  (1170 dofs) full 0.9920  B-bar 0.9972

L/H = 8, element aspect ratio 4:
  ny = 2  (30 dofs)   full 0.3328  B-bar 0.3421

So: 11.25 % too stiff at two square elements through the depth, and 66.7 % too stiff at aspect ratio 4. For comparison the Tri6 mesh of verification case 4 reaches 0.99930 on 1170 dofs.

B-BAR DOES NOT CURE IT, and this bead exists so that is not forgotten. B-bar lifts ny = 2 from 0.8875 to 0.9579, recovering about 63 % of the deficit and leaving 4.2 % missing; on the aspect-4 mesh it moves 0.3328 only to 0.3421. The share it recovers is the VOLUMETRIC part of the parasitic constraint (even at nu = 0 the bulk modulus is E/3, so bending excites a spurious dilatational stiffness). The share it does not recover is the parasitic SHEAR strain, a deviatoric mode B-bar leaves untouched by construction.

CANDIDATE FIXES, all a different family from B-bar and each needing its own verification: incompatible modes (Wilson), enhanced assumed strain (Simo-Rifai 1990), assumed natural strain, or reduced integration with hourglass control. Note quadrature.rs deliberately refuses plain reduced integration without stabilisation and that refusal should stand.

ACCEPTANCE: a Quad4 cantilever within 2 % of Timoshenko at two square elements through the depth AND within 10 % at element aspect ratio 4, with the patch test and the MMS convergence orders still passing (an enhanced-strain element must still pass the patch test - that is the whole point of Simo-Rifai's construction), plus the measured numbers recorded as case 8 records these.
title: Farrer Park: shear locking in Quad4 is measured but NOT cured
